manualNotes.text: The Go route inventory resolves literal r.Route prefixes and literal verb registrations in server/cmd/server/router.go. Computed paths, helper-owned routers, Mount/Handle registrations, build tags, and runtime conditionals require a manual override.

The database inventory replays CREATE/DROP declarations from ordered up migrations for tables, functions, triggers, and indexes. It does not connect to a running database, expand every inline constraint, or detect environment-specific schema drift.

Desktop paths are recovered from literal path properties in the appRoutes RouteObject tree. Index routes, Navigate targets, overlay transitions, and paths created outside that tree are not route literals.

Environment discovery covers literal and same-file constant Go os.Getenv/LookupEnv calls, common Go env helpers, Node process.env/import.meta.env access, Docker Compose template references, and .env.example declarations. Dynamically constructed names, general shell-script variables, CI secrets, and values are intentionally excluded.

Automatic external-I/O detection identifies concrete library and syscall primitives, not business semantics or delivery guarantees. Named external systems are maintained as evidence-backed manual overrides.

This generated inventory is a drift-checked architecture input. It does not replace maintained domain-flow documentation that connects UI/query keys through HTTP, handlers, services, SQL, events, failure recovery, and user-visible outcomes.
React Query counts are syntax-level call counts in production TypeScript sources. Wrapper hooks and aliased imports may hide calls; a call count is not a count of unique server-state domains.

Go-versus-TypeScript event differences and production reference sources are reported mechanically. Reference presence does not by itself distinguish producer from consumer; daemon/internal contracts and dynamic dispatch still require human classification.
